units.function: Pure tests for selecting a primary runtime API origin and constructing ordered callback candidates from preferred/public URLs, allowed hostnames, bind address, Docker host alias and reachable network interfaces.
units.dependencyDirection: Server deployment/auth/network configuration and OS interface discovery feed a runtime URL helper; local/SSH/sandbox Agent adapters consume the resulting origins to call back into the server.
units.keyDataModels: Preferred API URL; authentication public base URL; allowed hostname list; bind host/port; IPv4/IPv6 interface address/internal/link-local metadata; ordered candidate URL list.
units.lifecycle: Normalize explicit URLs to origins; prefer explicit then loopback choices; enumerate allowed/interface candidates; add a Docker host bridge for loopback; give runtimes multiple callback origins to attempt.
units.testAssessment: All 6 focused tests pass and clearly pin candidate precedence, loopback preference, Docker convenience, deduplication and link-local filtering. They do not establish transport identity or security. Non-loopback plaintext HTTP candidates are expected in some cases, auth public URL is reused as runtime API origin and no hostile URL/hostname, TLS, DNS, proxy, node identity or audience behavior is tested.
units.designRationale: Make local Agents, containers and SSH/private-network runtimes reach a single server across heterogeneous developer networking without requiring operators to configure a dedicated callback origin in every environment.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed-cloud plus customer-local execution requires reliable control/execution connectivity without exposing the control plane, sharing Web/identity tokens, or trusting network-discovered callback addresses across enterprise boundaries.
units.companyOsFit: NARROW to developer and explicit self-hosted bootstrap: loopback preference and link-local filtering are useful. Production/hybrid ExecutionNodes should initiate an authenticated outbound connection or reverse tunnel to a dedicated Runtime Gateway, register a stable opaque node identity/capability set and use mTLS or short-lived audience-bound tokens with rotation/revocation. Require TLS off-loopback, explicit allowlisted endpoints and separate Identity, customer Web and Runtime API origins. Never send ambient credentials while probing candidates.
units.responsibilityConflict: A runtime reaching the wrong origin can execute or report work under the wrong Company/Agent authority. Connectivity selection must bind node, tenant, Connector, work and token audience, and its attestation must be recorded without exposing network topology as responsibility evidence.

2026-08-19 focused Vitest: 1 file passed, 6/6 tests passed
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL transport risk if used in production: non-loopback callback candidates can be plaintext HTTP with no tested server/node authentication. HIGH trust-domain confusion: authPublicBaseUrl doubles as runtime API configuration even though identity and execution token audiences must differ. HIGH discovery risk: LAN/private/ULA and host.docker.internal candidates broaden reachable targets without tested allowlist/DNS-rebinding controls. HIGH URL gap: malformed schemes, embedded credentials, proxy path prefixes and IPv6 bracket serialization are untested. HIGH credential risk: no test ensures callback probing carries no ambient token to an unverified candidate. POSITIVE: loopback is preferred for local Agents and link-local addresses are filtered.
